ANDAMAN & NICOBAR ISLAND PRESS STUDY TOUR

Today, under the arrangement of the Information & Public Relations Department, 9 members of the Mizoram Journalist Association and 3 I&PR officials left Aizawl for a Press Study Tour to Andaman & Nicobar Island. Those taking part in the Press Study Tour to Andaman & Nicobar Island will study various government initiatives as well as meet government officials. The Press Study Tour is scheduled to be held from December 9, 2019 to December 15, 2019. The selected MJA members are from various districts of Mizoram, and they are being led by I&PR Director Pi Lallianpuii, MIS, and Joint Director (Admn) Pu C. Lalnunkima, MIS.

THE DRAFT ELECTORAL ROLL 2020 HAS BEEN PUBLISHED IN LAWNGTLAI

The draft electoral roll for the three Assembly constituencies in Lawngtlai District for the year 2020 was published yesterday (16.12.2019) in the office chamber of the Lawngtlai District Election Officer, who is also the Lawngtlai Deputy Commissioner, Pi Shashanka Ala, IAS. The draft roll was immediately handed over to representatives of political parties.

According to the published draft electoral roll, 36-Tuichawng (ST) A/C has 15,852 male voters and 15,520 female voters, making a total of 31,372; 37-Lawngtlai West (ST) A/C has 13,524 male voters and 13,402 female voters, making a total of 26,926; and 38-Lawngtlai East (ST) A/C has 11,626 male voters and 12,374 female voters, making a total of 24,000. Altogether, the three Assembly constituencies have 41,002 male voters and 41,296 female voters, making a total of 82,298 voters.

For the summary revision, time has been opened until January 15 of the new year for those who wish to make representations. The final electoral roll is scheduled to be published on February 7, 2020.

Along with this, 8 new polling stations will be added to the existing 62 polling stations in Tuichawng constituency, bringing the total to 70; 1 new polling station will be added to the existing 68 polling stations in Lawngtlai West, bringing the total to 69; and 7 new polling stations will be added to the existing 35 polling stations in Lawngtlai East, bringing the total to 42. Altogether, the three constituencies in Lawngtlai District will have 181 polling stations.

CHILDREN’S WEEK HELD IN MAMIT

Today, the District Child Protection Unit, Mamit District, organized a Fun Day programme at the GSA Playground, Mamit, as part of the opening of Children’s Week, using the theme “Happy Childhood.” Shashank Jaiswal, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Mamit, attended as the chief guest and expressed his gratitude to the District Child Protection Unit, Mamit, saying that the arrangements they made so that the children of Mamit could spend time happily were good and wise. He said that the safety and happiness of the children in our state are in everyone’s hands, and also emphasized the importance of cooperation among adults and the public, and the need for us to work together. He said that if the children in Mamit District face any difficulties, the Mamit Police will always be there to help them at any time. He urged the children to make use of the occasion to create happy and memorable moments, and invited everyone to use it as a means to further promote child protection. The programme was chaired by Vanlalruati, PO(IC), DCPU, and Dr. R. Lalrinhlua, DCPO, also spoke about why Fun Day was organized for the children in Mamit town and the importance of giving children more free and relaxed time. He said that since children are the future leaders of our country, it is our responsibility to care for them properly. During the Fun Day, the DCPU entertained the children with various fun activities such as Bouncy, Trampoline, See Saw, Mega Block, Ball Pool, and games like Spin the Wheel, Ball Kick, Dart Game, Cup Game, Ball Score, Photo Booth, Talent Hunt, and Bow and Arrow. Child Care Institutions also set up various stalls and presented these activities so that children could enjoy them free of cost. The children greatly valued the programme, and a large number of children from Mamit town attended.

hypothesis: Life was made to be defiled and ruined. For example, if we tell our children at home not to play with a blackboard eraser, then after I leave home, because they want to know for themselves, they play with the eraser; and when I come back, I find that they have done something wrong. Their wrongdoing is only a violation of family rules; nothing has entered into them. But if, on the other hand, we leave a box containing a dangerous poison at home and tell the children, “Do not touch this at all,” then after I leave home they find that the box is very pleasant to play with—and in the end they take in the dangerous poison. Here too, not only have they violated family rules and disobeyed my command, but something far worse and dangerous has entered into them. This is exactly what happened when Adam ate from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. He not only disobeyed God’s prohibition, but Satan’s life also entered into him. Then the inner life of man became utterly corrupted; along with the original good, right, and peaceful human life he had, he also came to possess Satan’s ruined and evil life.

source: COMMERCE & INDUSTRIES MINISTER-IN LUNGLEIAH AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING HAWNG No.4122/2021-2022 Aizawl, the 26 th February 2022 : Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana chuan vawiin khan Electric Veng, Lungleiah NABARD sum cheng nuai 1082.93 senga ruahman Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building a hawng. Hawnna inkhawm Commerce & Industries Department Commissioner & Secretary, Pi Esther Lal Ruatkimi kaihhruaiah Dr R Lalthangliana chuan Lunglei khawpui chhunga hmasawnna ruhrel liantham, khawtlang tana chhenfakawm tak leh eizawnna kawnga tangkai taka hman theih tur Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building zawhfel a ni chu lawmawm tiin a buaipuitu Commerce & Industries thawktute, building sa tu te leh Electric Veng Lunglei khawtlang te chungah lawmthu a sawi a. C&I Department hnuaiah hmalakna hrang hrang kalpui mek zel anih thu sawiin Lunglei Supermarket sakna tur cheng nuai 1400 NEC atanga sanction hmuh anih thu sawiin Bangladesh ram nena kan insumdawn tawnna atana ruahman Integrated Check Post (ICP), Kawrpuichhuah, Tlabung ti hlawhtling turin Department chuan theihtawp a chhuah mek zel thu a sawi a ni. A Department chan dangte hnuaia hmalaknte pawh sawilangin Minister chuan MZU Southern Campus atan DPR cheng vaibelchhe 400 sawrkar laipuiah thehluh tawh niin chak taka bawhzui mek a ni a, MZU Southern Campus tana hman lailawk tur Engineering College building chei that hna pawh thawh mek a ni, a ti a. Civil Hospital Lungleia Trauma Centre sak pawh zawh fel thuai beisei anih thu sawiin Multipurpose Laboratory Building, NEC sum cheng nuai 300 a ruahman mek pawh nakum kum tir lama zawhfel beisei anih thu a sawi. Lunglei Municipal Council (LMC) chungchang pawh sawiin Minister chuan Municipal body chak tak enkawlna hnuaiah Lunglei khawpui chuan kawng hrang hrangin hmasawnna a nei dawn a ni, a ti. He huna khualzahawm Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng chuan Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building hawn theiha peih fel a ni ta chu Pathian malsawmna ropui tak a ni tiin he hmasawnna ruhrel neih theihna tura sulsutute thawhrimna leh thahnemngaihna rah a ni, a ti a. He building ti hlawhtling tura bultan tu Pu Joseph Lalhimpuia chungah leh a hmun phal taka petu Electric Veng YMA te chungah lawmthu a sawi a ni. He building sak enkawltu AIE Constructions, Tuikhuahtlang, Aizawl atangin Technical Report ngaihtlak a ni a. Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure hi NABARD, RIDF XXIII hnuaia project niin total project cost hi Rs. 1082.93 lakhs ani a. Hna hi 05/10/2018 ah thawh tan a ni. A building plinth area hi 574.875 Square metres niin building hi floor nga (5) a sak a ni a. First floor hi Agriculture leh marketing lama training leh awareness centre atan ruahman niin mihring 300 vel leng tura hisap a ni. Ground floor ah hian guest room, conference/meeting room te awmin Basement I ah hian mi 78 lenna market area bakah market office ruamhan niin Basement II ah mi 85 lenna market area niin Basement III hi motor 25 lenna parking area-a ruahman a ni. reference: AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING INAUGURATED AT LUNGLEI No.523/2021-2022 Aizawl, the 28th February 2022 : Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana on Saturday (26th February, 2022) inaugurated Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building at Electric Veng, Lunglei. The Rs. 1082.93 lakhs project is implemented under the NABARD, RIDF XXIII. Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng was the guest of honour at the inauguration. At the inaugural function chaired by Commerce & Industries Department Commissioner & Secretary, Pi Esther Lal Ruatkimi, Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana commended C&I Department staff, Electric veng YMA, VCs for their contribution towards successful completion of the project. As per Technical Report presented by AIE Constructions, Tuikhuahtlang, Aizawl, the 5 floors Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building has a plinth area of 574.875 Square metres. The first floor is intended to be used as a training and awareness centre for agriculture marketing with an estimated capacity of 300 people, with guest rooms, conference/meeting rooms at the Ground floor. Basement I and Basement II contain the market areas and market offices, with a parking area at the basement.

raw_text:
COMMERCE & INDUSTRIES MINISTER INAUGURATES AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING IN LUNGLEI

No. 4122/2021-2022  
Aizawl, 26th February 2022: Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr. R. Lalthangliana today inaugurated the Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building at Electric Veng, Lunglei, constructed at a cost of Rs. 1082.93 lakh from NABARD funds.

At the inauguration ceremony, held under the chairmanship of Commerce & Industries Department Commissioner & Secretary, Pi Esther Lal Ruatkimi, Dr. R. Lalthangliana said he was pleased that the Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building, a major development structure within Lunglei town and one that would be highly useful to the community and for livelihood activities, had been completed. He expressed gratitude to the officials of the Commerce & Industries Department who worked on the project, the builders, and the people of Electric Veng, Lunglei.

Speaking about the various ongoing initiatives under the C&I Department, he said that sanction for Rs. 1400 lakh from NEC for the construction of Lunglei Supermarket had been received, and that the Department was making every effort to ensure the success of the Integrated Check Post (ICP) at Kawrpuichhuah, Tlabung, which has been planned to facilitate trade with Bangladesh.

Mentioning other projects under his department, the Minister said that the DPR for the MZU Southern Campus, amounting to Rs. 400 crore, had already been submitted to the Central Government and was being pursued vigorously. He added that renovation work on the Engineering College building, which would be used for the MZU Southern Campus, was also underway. He further said that the Trauma Centre at Civil Hospital, Lunglei, was expected to be completed soon, and that the Multipurpose Laboratory Building, planned at a cost of Rs. 300 lakh from NEC funds, was also expected to be completed early next year.

Speaking also about the Lunglei Municipal Council (LMC), the Minister said that under the efficient administration of the municipal body, Lunglei town would see development in various fields.

RAJYA SABHA MP K. VANLALVENA BRINGS THE PLIGHT OF THE PEOPLE OF MYANMAR TO THE INDIA VICE PRESIDENT

No. 7795/2020-2021  
Aizawl, 15th March, 2021: Rajya Sabha MP Pu K. Vanlalvena, who is currently in Delhi for the Parliament Budget Session, met India’s Vice President, who is also the Rajya Sabha Chairman, Pu M. Venkaiah Naidu, at his residence today and discussed the severe suffering being faced by those who are working to restore democracy in Myanmar, as well as other important issues concerning Mizoram.

Pu Vena was accompanied by MNF Adviser Pu Rosangzuala. He informed the Vice President that due to the unrest in Myanmar, many people have already been killed and injured at the hands of the military, many have been imprisoned, and the exact number of those killed and injured cannot yet be known, with the toll likely to continue rising. He also told him that some members of the Myanmar military and police, unwilling to use force against the people of Myanmar, have surrendered their weapons and, together with some other civilians, have already fled into Mizoram seeking refuge.

He further conveyed that arrangements for the care and support of those who have entered from Myanmar need to be considered, and urged the India Vice President to take necessary steps to help end the suffering of the people of Myanmar. He also said that the central government’s policy toward Myanmar needs to be reviewed.

Pu Vena and Pu Rosangzuala also requested the Vice President to support efforts to ensure that a Mizo is appointed to the Union Public Service Commission, since after India’s independence no person from Mizoram has ever been a member of the UPSC. They told him that even after 35 years as a full-fledged state, Mizoram is still under the AGMUT cadre in the All India Civil Services, and that it is now time to create a separate Mizoram cadre. They also urged Pu M. Venkaiah Naidu to consider allowing candidates applying for jobs under the Staff Selection Commission to take examinations in Aizawl instead of having to go all the way to Guwahati.

Under Kawrthah VDVK Centre targetted beneficiaries of 300 tribal women from Kawrthah cluster will be trained in tailoring. hypothesis: VDVK LEVEL ADVOCACY PROGRAMME HELD UNDER PMVDY IN KAWRTHAH
raw_text:
VDVK LEVEL ADVOCACY PROGRAMME HELD UNDER PMVDY IN KAWRTHAH

No.2537/2021-2022  
Aizawl, 8th October, 2021: Today in Kawrthah village, under the Pradhan Mantri Vandhan Yojana (PMVDY), a Vandhan Vikas Kendra (VDVK) Level Advocacy Programme, Entrepreneurship and Skill Development Programme training was held. Pu Lalthangfala, District Cooperative Officer, Mamit, was the chief guest and inaugurated the programme. The chief guest said that a weaving training center for Mizo women has been opened at the VDVK Center in Kawrthah village and that weaving machines will be distributed under the Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana (PMVDY). He urged those undergoing weaving training to work hard and train themselves in a way that would be useful for earning a livelihood. Today, following Covid Appropriate Behaviour, this awareness programme was held in one batch with 40 participants out of 300 women interested in weaving.

raw_text:
LUNGLEI DISTRICT - COVID-19 NO TOLERANCE FORTNIGHT No.6374/2020-2021

The Mizoram Government’s planned “Covid-19 No Tolerance Fortnight,” intended to curb the rapid spread of the Covid-19 pandemic and to encourage the public to adopt the preventive measures put in place against Covid-19 as a way of life, is being strictly implemented in Lunglei District from October 26 to November 9, 2020. Along with this, the Jan Andolan Campaign for awareness on Covid-19 safety is also being continued.

Yesterday, under the chairmanship of Lunglei DC & DLTF Chairman Pu V. Lalsangliana, a meeting was held in his office chamber and the detailed implementation of the Covid-19 No Tolerance Fortnight in Lunglei District was discussed. During the No Tolerance Fortnight, 30 personnel from each government department assigned for Covid-19 Executive Duty were divided into 24 teams, and their duty arrangements were finalized. Each team has a Team Leader, and the public will be widely informed about the Covid-19 preventive guidelines; those who do not follow the instructions will be fined without any leniency.

The Covid-19 Executive Duty personnel are strictly enforcing the provisions of The Mizoram (Containment and Prevention of Spread of Covid-19) Act, 2020, which requires the public to comply, as well as all government orders issued. Banners on Covid-19 preventive measures have also been displayed at important locations in Lunglei town. The VLTFs have also been requested to broadcast Covid-19 preventive measures and guidelines three times daily in their respective localities/villages.

hypothesis: Throughout the world there is at least one chosen person of God who can say this: “The ruler of this world is coming, and he has no claim on me” (John 14:30). In other words, in the Lord Jesus there was not even a trace of this world’s ruler. What we must carefully note is that when the Lord Jesus came into this world, He did not come as God, but as man. God needed man. If God Himself were to deal with Satan, it would be easy enough; Satan would immediately fall without a struggle. But God did not intend to do that. To deal with Satan, He wanted man; He intended to have the creature deal with the creature. When the Lord Jesus came in the form of man, He suffered temptation as a man and experienced everything that human beings experience. This man overcame, and this man is the Victor. He ascended and sat at the right hand of God. Jesus was “crowned with glory and honor” (Heb. 2:9); He has been glorified.
raw_text: Throughout the world there is at least one chosen person of God who can say this: “The ruler of this world is coming, and he has no claim on me” (John 14:30). God needed man. If God Himself were to deal with Satan, it would be easy enough; Satan would immediately fall without a struggle. But God did not intend to do that. To deal with Satan, He wanted man; He intended to have the creature deal with the creature. When the Lord Jesus came in the form of man, He suffered temptation as a man and experienced everything that human beings experience. This man overcame, and this man is the Victor. He ascended and sat at the right hand of God. Jesus was “crowned with glory and honor” (Heb. 2:9); He has been glorified.

reference: MIZORAM CHIEF SECRETARY LEADS GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES IN TAKING INTEGRITY PLEDGE 275/2023-2024 Vigilance Awareness Week, 2023 is to be observed in the whole of India from today, i.e. 30th October till 5th November, 2023. This year the theme is - 'Say no to corruption, commit to the Nation'. Starting off the Vigilance Week in Mizoram too, Chief Secretary Dr. Renu Sharma led the officials and staff of the Mizoram Secretariat, MINECO this morning in taking the 'Integrity Pledge' in the Secretariat Courtyard. Likewise, all Heads of Offices under the State Government also led the employees in their respective offices in taking the Integrity Pledge, in which each government servant avowed to follow probity and rule of law in all walks of life, to neither take nor offer bribe, to perform all tasks in an honest and transparent manner, to act in public interest, to lead by example exhibiting integrity in personal behavior and to report any incident of corruption to the appropriate agency. hypothesis: Under the leadership of Mizoram Chief Secretary, the Integrity Pledge was taken together in connection with the observance of Vigilance Awareness Week 2023, from 30th October to 5th November, 2023, across India. This year’s Vigilance Week theme is “Say no to corruption, commit to the Nation.” Along with other parts of the country, this morning in Mizoram too, in order to inaugurate “Vigilance Week 2023,” all government employees, officials, and staff at the Mizoram Secretariat, MINECO, took the “Integrity Pledge” together under the leadership of Chief Secretary Dr. Renu Sharma. Heads of Offices in every government office also took the “Integrity Pledge” together with the officers and staff working under them at their respective office premises. Through this Integrity Pledge, they vowed that every government employee must firmly oppose corruption, work honestly and transparently in accordance with government rules and orders, and, recognizing that public service is their duty, conduct themselves and perform their work in a humble manner worthy of emulation by others; and that if they see or become aware of any corrupt practice, they should not remain silent but must report it to the government.

Aspirational District atangin Mizoram District 11- te zingah pakhatna ni thei tura tan la tura chahin in tum tlat chuan theihloh a awm lo a ni tiin kum zabi 21-a hmasawnna chu hmang tangkaiin dik taka kan hmachhawn chuan District hnufual ber thin kha a ropui ber kan ni thei a ni a ti. VAILIAM No.7589/2020-2021

Today, Dr. R. Lalthangliana, Minister of the Health & Family Welfare Department, Higher & Technical Education, and Commerce & Industries, handed over a Mobile Medical Van, Essential Drugs & Diagnostic Kits, and laptops and speakers to be used at Mamit District Hospital, PHC/CHC, and Sub-Centres.

Lalthangliana said he was very pleased that such useful equipment had been provided so that the people living in Mamit District could make progress in the field of health. He said that among the 11 districts, Mamit has a District Bawrhsap who truly understands the importance of health, and that they are very fortunate. He added that if they are determined to work hard so as to become number one among Mizoram’s 11 districts from among the Aspirational Districts, nothing is impossible. He said that if we make proper use of the progress of the 21st century and face it correctly, the district that has usually been the most backward can become the most glorious.

Dr. Thangtea said that being a Mizo who believes in God is a blessing, and that because we have always worked together in unity and harmony handed down from our ancestors, good results continue to emerge. Although it is deeply unfortunate that we have lost lives due to Covid-19, he said that our success in the fight against the disease, and the fact that Mizoram has the lowest number of Covid-19 deaths among the eight states of Northeast India, is due to God and our cooperation.

The Minister urged the gathering not to be satisfied merely with the progress already achieved, but to continue striving with renewed effort so that we may achieve comprehensive development. He also said that work is underway to build good roads, and that road construction from the eastern side toward the western side has begun.

Er. H. Lalzirliana, the local MLA, also said that it was a matter of joy that useful equipment had been purchased under CSR so that Mamit District could make progress in health care and emerge from being an Aspirational District. raw_text:
HEALTH MINISTER ATTENDS IMA MIZORAM BRANCH CONFERENCE

Today, the Indian Medical Association (IMA) Mizoram State Branch held its 43rd Annual Conference at Aijal Club. Dr. R. Lalthangliana, Health Minister, was the chief guest. The theme of this year’s IMA Annual Conference was “Ending the HIV & AIDS Epidemic: Community by Community.”

Dr. R. Lalthangliana said that the government gives importance to the health sector, and that health has been given a major place even in SEDP, the main initiative of the Mizoram government. He said the government is open to improving healthcare and has been making serious efforts to build the infrastructure for progress. The Minister said the government is making every possible effort in all areas of development, including the construction of a Cancer Super Speciality Hospital at Zemabawk, strengthening ZMC, the development of RIPANS, and the advancement of various hospitals and health-related sectors across Mizoram.

Dr. R. Lalthangliana said doctors and nurses are servants of the people and workers performing important and honorable duties, and urged them to continue dedicating themselves to this service, reminding them that beyond medical knowledge, even a kind word can bring healing to the sick.

The opening programme of the conference was chaired by IMA President Dr. Rosangliana, and Honorary Secretary Dr. Chawnglungmuana presented reports on the various activities of the association. The IMA Mizoram State Branch has 33 members and also has 15 new intern members. Among its existing members, 15 are newly qualified specialists (MD/MS). During the year, it received the IMA Special Award for Organizing (IMA North East Leaders Meet Conclave) and the President Appreciation Award (for IMA Membership Drive Trophy) from IMA Headquarters.

The association regularly organizes Special Clinics in rural areas, where patients are treated free of charge with various equipment and supplies. To promote progress in medical knowledge, it regularly arranges various seminars for its members, and in this conference as well, HIV and AIDS were studied in detail.

GOVT. ITI, AIZAWL HOLDS CONVOCATION 1974/2022-2023

Aizawl, 17th September, 2022: Today, at Govt. ITI, Aizawl, for the first time in Mizoram, a convocation programme was held for 143 ITI graduates. Govt. ITI Aizawl currently has 384 students in the ongoing 2022–23 session, and in the latest result it recorded an overall pass percentage of 97.14%. Since its establishment, Govt. ITI, Aizawl has been among the best-performing Govt. ITIs in India, and in Mizoram it has secured the sixth position among the various states in the country.

At the convocation, certificates were awarded to 143 students. In the convocation programme, Pu K. Lalhmingliana, Director, LESDE Department, delivered the welcome address and expressed gratitude for the success of the graduating students, who will help Mizoram’s skills sector continue to advance. The chief guest, Pu Lalramsanga Sailo, Secretary, LESDE Department, said that he was very pleased that ITI education in Mizoram is progressing steadily and that Mizo youth are taking a keen interest in skill-based learning. He also said it was a matter of pride that Govt. ITI, Aizawl could be among the best-performing institutions with excellent results among the top government ITIs in India. He further stated that, for the state to continue progressing and for youth to be able to stand on their own through skills, it is important to further strengthen ITIs.

Most of the technicians working in Mizoram are graduates of Govt. ITI, Aizawl, and among the ITI graduates, 14 students from the Motor Mechanic Vehicle (MMV) trade received offer letters from large companies even before the results were announced. Convocation had never before been held on a state-wide basis, and under the arrangement of the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE), it has been introduced from this year. Convocation programmes were held simultaneously in various parts of India, with the main event taking place in Delhi under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and the convocation is planned to be held every year in connection with Vishwakarma Diwas (Day).

The final electoral rolls to be used for the Tokalo MDC constituency by-election were released

At 1:00 PM yesterday (15.10.2019), District Election Officer and Deputy Commissioner Pu Bhupesh Chaudhary, IAS, released the final electoral rolls to be used for the Tokalo Constituency MDC by-election in his office chamber, and handed over hard and soft copies of the final rolls to representatives of various political parties.

The by-election is being held due to the death of Tokalo constituency MDC Pu K.L. Bana. Using 1st January, 2019 as the qualifying date, the summary revision of the electoral rolls was carried out smoothly as planned by the State Election Commission, and today was fixed for the release of the final electoral rolls.

Those present at the release of the final electoral rolls included Pu K. Vanlalthiana, Addl. DC; Pu Amol Srivastava, IAS, Asst. Commissioner; Pu H. Zonunmawia, Election Officer; Pu N. Vabeiratlua, DIPRO; representatives of Tlawmngai Pawl MTP(H) and MCHP(H); and representatives of various political parties.

According to the draft electoral rolls released earlier, there were 450 female voters and 505 male voters in 1-Tokalo constituency, making a total of 955 voters.

SPORTS MINISTER HONORS NES U-19 TEAM

A felicitation programme was held today at Loch Hall, 46 Assam Rifles, at the headquarters of Sector 23 Assam Rifles, to honor the Mizoram team that recently became champions of the NES Under-19 Women Football Championship. The event was attended by Sports Minister Pu Robert Romawia Royte. Leaders of the Mizoram Football Association (MFA) were also present.

Speaking at the event, Sports Minister Pu Robert Romawia Royte congratulated the Mizoram Under-19 Women’s Team on becoming champions of the NES U-19 Championship and said that this victory does not belong to the government, nor to the organizers and hosts Assam Rifles, nor to the MFA, but to the people of Mizoram. He said the team has made the people of Mizoram proud.

He said that by defeating the Nagaland women’s team, which had recently represented India at the international level, the Mizoram women’s team had shown how strong Mizoram’s women footballers are. He added that the government would continue to support and strengthen the efforts of the MFA for the growth of football, and called on MFA leaders to continue the good cooperation between the government and the MFA.

Pu Robert Romawia Royte said football is a very important tool for national unity and strengthening bonds, and because of football, the Northeast states and other parts of India are connecting better, creating a more harmonious atmosphere and strengthening national integration. He said the possibilities in football are great and should not be underestimated.

He said that since the government wants to promote sports disciplines other than football more strongly than before, the Mizoram Sports Policy, which Mizoram has never had before, is currently being prepared. He said the development of taekwondo, basketball, volleyball and other sports disciplines is encouraging, and the government is thinking about ways to strengthen sports associations. As Sports Minister, he said he would do his utmost to ensure better management.

He also said that efforts are underway to install proper floodlights at Rajiv Gandhi Sports Stadium so that international-level matches can be held there, and that sites are being identified to build about four or five more football fields in Aizawl city. He added that sanction has already been received for laying grass at Zembawk field, and plans are also being made to lay grass at Khawzawl field.

source: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati in Sainik School Chhingchhip a tlawh 2122/2022-2023 Chhingchhip, the 30th September 2022: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati chuan vawiin khan Sainik School Chhingchhip a tlawh a. He hunah hian School building leh hmunhma te a endik a, Sikul naupangte hmaah fuihna thu a sawi bawk a ni. Governor hian Sainik School a thlenin amah zahna chibai 8 Bn Assam Rifles ten School kawtah an lo buk a. Wcdr Shahul Hameed, Principal leh Maj S.Kalyan, Administrative Officer ten zirtirtute leh School staff te an hmelhriattir chhunzawm a. Hemi zawh hian Principal Office ah Sainik School dinhmunte inhrilhhriatna hun neih leh a ni a. Assembly Hall-ah Official programme leh Cultural Programme neih chhunzawm nghal a ni. Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati chuan Principal leh a thawhpui ten Sainik School tha tak ni tur leh hmun danga Sainik School te dinhmun pha tura theihtawp an chhuah chu fakawm a tih thu a sawi hmasa a. Mizoram sawrkarin hetiang ang School tha bik Mizorama zirlaite tan a buatsaih thei chu lawmawm a tih thu a sawi bawk a ni. Sainik School Chhingchhip hi India ram hmundang te aia a danglam bik na chu helai hmunah hian Sainik School dangte entawn turin a vawikhatna atana leh a hmahruaitu ni turin hmeichhe naupangte luh tir an ni a. Hei hi a chhuanawm tak zet a ni a ti. Sainik School te hi khawi hmunah pawh School thabik an ni a, Sipai, Navy leh Airforce Officer ni turin a bik takin heng schoolah te hian zirlai te zirtirna pek a ni a ti. Sainik School a zirlaite hi Armed Forces ah an thawkvek kher lo a nih pawhin khawtlang leh ram tana khua leh tui entawn tlak ni tura chher an nih thu a sawi bawk. India chakna chu danglamna tam tak kara inpumkhatna leh inunauna tha a ni tih zirlaite chu a hrilh nawn leh a. He mawhphurhna huangah hian Sainik School zirlaite chu hmahruaitu ni turin a chah a ni. reference: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati visits Sainik School Chhingchhip 191/2022-2023 Chhingchhip, the 30th September 2022: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati who is on an official tour of Serchhip District visited Sainik School, Chhingchhip, a few miles away from Serchhip town today. Upon his arrival, Governor was accorded the Guard of Honour by 8 Bn of Assam Rifles. He was then introduced to the staff by Wcdr Shahul Hameed, Principal, and Maj S.Kalyan, Administrative Officer. A briefing about the School to Governor was given by the Principal in his office room. After this, an official function with a cultural program was organized inside the Assembly Hall in honour of the esteemed visitor. Here, the Governor addressed the students. Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati congratulated faculties for their best effort to keep up with other establishwd Sainik Schools in the country. He thanked the state government for bring up a highly valuable asset of national importance in education like Sainik school here in Mizoram. He expressed his pride of having the first Sainik School in the country where girl students are admitted. He stressed the importance of Sainik Schools for preparing the young students to become cadet officers in Army, Airforces and Navy. Beside this, he said the school also prepared the students to become role model students and role model citizen. He reminded the students of the school about their important duties for the national integration of the county. Full speech of the Honble Governor : https://dipr.mizoram.gov.in/post/speech-of-dr-hari-babu-kambhampati-honble-governor-of-mizoram-on-the-occasion-of-visit-to-sainik-school-chhingchhip-on-30th-september-2022 The programme began with welcome address by Maj S.Kalyan, Admn and concluded with vote of thanks proposed by WCdr Shahul Hameed, Principal, Sainik School, Chhingchhip. After the official programme, Governor inspected the facilities inside the campus of Sainik School Chhingchhip. As per the briefing by the Principal, here are the few highlights of the school. The school is now 6 years old and running with the pilot cadets in Class XI. The annual intake of students are 60 boys and 10 girls in the class VI while in the class IX only boys are admitted with the availability of 10 seats for students annually. The annual fee per a student is estimated at Rs 1.85 lakh per year. The schools have daily routine for winter and summer and winter with the physical and classroom activities through out the day. It usually starts from very early morning till 9:00 to 9:30 PM at night. Apart from the facilities for cocurricular activities, the School is also currently having the facilities like Football Ground, Badminton Court, Basketball Court, Gynasium, Music room,etc.,. The swimming pool, parade ground and other big sports facilities are being planned to be added very soon. The Principal highlighted the status of Grant in Aid from the state, issues with water and power bills, LMV ambulance to be received from the Mizoram Rural Bank through CSR, INSAS rifles to be received from Home Department, Government of Mizoram, Infrastructural Fund received to the tune of Rs 99,96,000 the Ministry of Defence with the proposed implementations. To solve the issue with high power bills, the Governor advised implementation of Solar Power Generation plant inside the campus. While, the issue with high water bills is being taken up the office Deputy Commissioner and is expected to be solved very soon. Governor in his visit to Sainik School, Chhingchhip was escorted and given a company by Pu Lalmuansanga Ralte, Addl DC and Pu Stephen Lalrinawma, SP, Serchhip District. Chutiang bawkin Synod Office leh a hnuaia Department hrang hrangten office mamawh (stationeries) an neihte chu a theih hrâm chuan Synod Bookroom-a mi lei tûra tih a ni a, Synod Bookroom-in an pêk theih loh thu an ziak thilte chauh hmun danga lei tûra tih a ni {Synod Sum Vawn Dân Bung 10:10 (1)}.
reference: The main objectives of the Presbyterian Communication Board/Department is to spread the Gospel through publication and printing words and it is responsible for the publication of any works required by Synod and all the departments under it. It also provides cheaper and accessible books for the masses as well. Synod and its departments are to publish their books and any other publication under Synod Press. (SEC 233:39). Similarly, all the departments are to buy their stationary needs from the Synod Bookroom as well. {Synod Sum VawnDân Bung 10:10 (1)}.
hypothesis: The main work of the Presbyterian Communications Board/Department is to ensure that the ministry of the written word continues to advance. Therefore, whatever materials the Synod and its various departments need to have printed should be properly printed, and among them, those suitable for sale should be sold at the lowest possible price so that the public can buy them. Books and other materials that the various departments under the Synod need to have printed are to be printed at the Synod Press (SEC 233:39). Likewise, office supplies needed by the Synod Office and the various departments under it are, as far as possible, to be purchased from the Synod Bookroom, and only those items that the Synod Bookroom cannot provide are to be bought elsewhere {Synod Sum Vawn Dân Bung 10:10 (1)}.

reference: ASSAM RIFLES BATTALION TO CONDUCT 8TH ROZGAR MELA FOR MIZORAM STATE 195/2023-2024 Aizawl the 26th August, 2023 - Battalion of Headquarters Inspector General Assam Rifles (East) will be conducting 8th Rozgar Mela on 28 August 2023 at 2 AR Gajraj Hall, Lakhimpur Battalion. A large number of individuals will be benefitted by the Mela. Central Government is set to organize the 8th Job Fair on 28 August 2023. This event, spanning over 25 states and more than 44 locations, will see the distribution of appointment letters to approximately 70,000 young individuals of various Departments of the Indian Government. Notably, our Honorable Prime Minister Narendra Modi will preside over the event, addressing the youth through live streaming, followed by the distribution of appointment letter to the candidates present. Assam Rifles is playing a pivotal role in organizing the Rozgar Mela for the state of Mizoram and overseeing the eventâ€™s coordination. The Honorable Minister of Minority Affairs, Mr John Barla will personally hand over appointment letter to the candidates. The Honorable Prime Minister will witness the ceremony via Video Conferencing. The Rozgar Mela is a step towards fulfillment of the duty of Government to accord highest priority to employment generation.

According to the Central Government’s plan, the Rozgar Mela/Job Fair will be held on Monday, August 28, at 44 locations in 25 states. During this event, appointment letters will be distributed to nearly 70,000 newly recruited employees in various departments under the Government of India. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will lead the nationwide event and, after addressing the youth through live streaming, will distribute appointment letters to the newly recruited employees present at the venue. In order to ensure the successful organization of the Rozgar Mela/Job Fair in Mizoram, Assam Rifles has taken the initiative, and the event will be graced by Union Minister of State for Minority Affairs John Barla, who will hand over appointment letters to the new recruits. The Prime Minister will also attend the events held at various places across the country through video conferencing. The Rozgar Mela is an important initiative of the Central Government aimed at creating employment opportunities for the unemployed.

A. Chhûnglama Chenchilhtu Thlarau Angin
Pathianin kan chhûngah a thlarau a dah a, tichuan a thlarau chu kan chhûngah chenchilhtu Thlarau a ni ang a, Pathian hriatna leh Pathian lama Krista-in kan tâna a hlenchhuah zawng zawng tawnhriatna kan nei thei dawn a ni (Rom 8:9-11). Hei hi Thuthlung Thar huna malsawmna danglam bik Pathianin a pêk chu a ni a; Thuthlung Hluiah a awm rêng rêng lo a ni. Thuthlung Hluiah chuan Pathian chuan a Thlarau chu pawnlama mihring chunga hnathawk tur ringawtin a siam a, mihring chhûngah chuan a Thlarau chu chenchilh turin a siam lo a ni. Lalpa thihna leh thawhlehna hnuah chauh chuan Pathian chuan a Thlarau chu kan hnenah min pe in, chenchilhtu Thlarau angin Thlarau chu kan chhûnga nung turin a siam a (John. 14:16-17). Hei vâng hian kan chhûnglam aṭangin Pathian leh Krista chu a puangchhuak thei a, tichuan Pathian khahna chu keini Krista ami ten kan lo dawn a kan chen theihna turin a ni (Kol. 2:9-10).
reference:
A. As the Indwelling Spirit
God puts His Spirit in us so that His Spirit may be the indwellingSpiritwithinus,thatwemayknowGodandexpe- rience all that God in Christ has accomplished for us (Rom. 8:9-11). This is the special blessing given by God in the New Testament era; it did not exist in the Old Testament. In the OldTestament,GodonlycausedHisSpirittocomefromwith- out to work upon man; He did not cause His Spirit to dwell withinman. Only after the Lord’s death and resurrection did God give His Spirit to us and cause His Spirit to dwell in us as the indwelling Spirit (John 14:16-17). Thus, He is able to reveal both God and Christ to us from within,that we in Christ may receive and enjoy the fullness of God (Col. 2:9-10).
hypothesis: A. As the Spirit Dwelling Within
raw_text:
A. As the Spirit Dwelling Within

God has placed His Spirit within us, so that His Spirit becomes the indwelling Spirit in us, and we can have the experiential knowledge of all that Christ has accomplished for us in relation to God and the knowledge of God (Rom. 8:9-11). This is God’s special blessing in the New Testament age; it was not found at all in the Old Testament. In the Old Testament, God arranged for His Spirit only to work upon people outwardly; He did not arrange for His Spirit to dwell within people. Only after the Lord’s death and resurrection did God give us His Spirit and make the Spirit dwell within us as the indwelling Spirit (John 14:16-17). Because of this, from within us God and Christ can be expressed, and thus the fullness of God is for us who are in Christ to receive and to live by (Col. 2:9-10).

reference: In the Scriptures, only 1 John 2:27 speaks of the “teach- ing of the anointing.” We all know that anointing is a verbal noun which refers to the activity of the ointment, the mov- ing and the working of the ointment.According to the type of the Old Testament and the fulfillment of the New Testa- ment, ointment or oil in the Scripture refers to the Holy Spirit(Isa.61:1;Luke4:18).Sinceointmentoroilreferstothe Holy Spirit, the “anointing” must refer to the working of the Holy Spirit. The working of the Holy Spirit in us is like the anointing of the ointment; therefore, the Scripture calls this working of the Holy Spirit the “anointing.”
hypothesis: In the Bible, 1 John 2:27 speaks of “the anointing’s teaching.” Anointing refers to the act of anointing with oil, the practice of applying oil, and the work that this anointing signifies. Since the mixed oil or oil represents the Holy Spirit, “anointing” surely refers to the work of the Holy Spirit. The work of the Holy Spirit within us is like the anointing with mixed oil; therefore, the Bible calls the work of the Holy Spirit “anointing.”

reference: Let me also state that people must not rush to push the government to provide for their needs. So, time management is the most important key. I think the way files are processed hierarchy-wise also needs to be revised to save more time.

raw_text:
Under the chairmanship of the HPC Vice Chairman, a felicitation program was held today at the Lunglei BDO Conference Hall for the medal winners from the Lunglei East Assembly Constituency in the Mizoram State Games 2019, which was concluded in December last year, under the leadership of Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng, who is both the MLA of Lunglei East AC and Vice Chairman of the Lunglei HPC.

In the Mizoram State Games 2019, Lunglei East AC won 23 medals in various sports disciplines—7 gold, 7 silver, and 9 bronze—ranking 11th in Mizoram overall; in Lunglei District, they stood first.

Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng said he was pleased that Lunglei East AC was able to secure such a good position in the Mizoram State Games 2019, and expressed his gratitude to the members of the Organizing Committee, the athletes, and the party leaders, saying it was the result of their hard work and dedication. He encouraged the athletes to continue striving to guide their younger peers in a positive way and to keep working hard so that they can achieve success not only at the state level but also at the national and international levels. He also urged them to pay attention to and carefully study the various welfare schemes the government has arranged for athletes.

The athletes honored today were medal winners in different sports disciplines, and they were presented with citations and cash awards.

Lunglei East AC won 23 medals in 19 of the 32 sports disciplines included in the Mizoram State Games—7 gold, 7 silver, and 9 bronze—ranking 11th in Mizoram overall; in Lunglei District, they stood first.

Gold Medal – Citation + Rs. 4000/-
Silver Medal – Citation + Rs. 3000/-
Bronze Medal – Citation + Rs. 2000/-

CHAMPHAI CLEANLINESS WEEK 2021 CONCLUDES

No.2543/2021-2022
Aizawl, 8th October, 2021: Cleanliness Week 2021, held from October 2 to 8 under the theme “Cleanliness - From our homes and surroundings,” concluded this afternoon at 2:00 pm at the Horticulture Complex, New Champhai. On this occasion, District Superintendent Pi Maria C.T. Zuali was the chief guest, and prizes were distributed to the winners of various cleanliness competitions. The chief guest, Pi Maria C.T. Zuali, said that work for cleanliness should not end after the week is over, but should be practiced throughout the year. She said that if every household takes responsibility and spends at least one hour every day focusing on cleanliness, Champhai District can become the cleanest and most hygienic district. She urged the people of the district to do their best to keep Champhai District clean and protected, as it has pleasant weather, beautiful and green surroundings, lovely paddy fields, and many attractive places that other districts do not have. Speaking about preserving the beauty and pleasantness of Champhai, she said that the people living here themselves are the most important, and since we ourselves are often the ones who litter, we should not throw garbage carelessly when we go to the town and its beautiful surroundings. She also said that dustbins should be installed in all important and crowded places, and if we continue to teach cleanliness seriously in schools, clubs, localities, offices, and churches, we will be able to make great progress. Lalthlangliana, District Election Officer, with the Electoral Registration Officer, Assistant Electoral Registration Officer, representatives of various political parties, and members of the District Level Standing Committee in attendance.

CHIEF MINISTER ATTENDS GRADUATION AND LAMP LIGHTING CEREMONY AT RIPANS

Today, Chief Minister Pu Zoramthanga attended as chief guest the graduation ceremony for newly passed students from various Nursing and Paramedical courses this year, and the Lamp Lighting Ceremony for 35 first-year Bachelor of Nursing students at the Regional Institute of Paramedical and Nursing Sciences (RIPANS). He also presented Proficiency Awards to the most outstanding students.

The Chief Minister said he was happy for the new graduates. He said that using their skills to serve others and work in healthcare is a noble profession, and he wished the newly passed students would continue to work diligently and faithfully in their future endeavors and keep moving toward success.

The Chief Minister said the government gives importance to improving healthcare and providing better medical services in Mizoram. For this, he said, the government alone cannot do everything, and if the state is truly to make progress in the field of health, public cooperation is needed.

The Chief Minister said he was pleased with the ongoing efforts to make RIPANS more advanced, and he said the government would do its utmost to address the difficulties caused by staff shortages.

The Chief Minister also presented the RIPANS Proficiency Award to the most outstanding students among the new graduates in their respective departments.

At today’s event, RIPANS Director Dr. Chawngthanliana and Lamp Lighter Civil Hospital Nursing Superintendent Pi Lalrinthangi also spoke.

The 35 students present today were first-year B.Sc. Nursing students. RIPANS Director Dr. Chawngthanliana presented Certificates of Appreciation to the new Graduate and Post Graduate students. This year, a total of 180 students graduated, namely:
i) B.Sc. Nursing - 36
ii) B.Sc. MLT (Medical Laboratory Technology) - 40

iv) B. Optometry - 34
v) B.Sc. RIT (Radio Imaging Technology) - 31
vi) M. Pharm - 16

source: GOVERNOR PU HARI BABU KAMBHAMPATI IN CHAMPHAI WINERY TLAWH, PMUY LEH PMAY-HFA URBAN HAMTHATNA DAWNGTUTE TLAWHIN A KAWM 3449/2022-2023 Champhai, the 1st February, 2023: Ni hnih cham tura Champhai tlawha thang mek Mizoram Governor Pu Hari Babu Kambhampati chuan vawiin chawhnu khan Champhai Winery, Tlangsam tlawhin an hmalaknate a enfiah a; Champhal Grape Growers Society leh Hnahlan Grape Growers and Processing Co-operative Society Limited hotute a kawm bawk. Hemi hnu hian Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) leh Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Housing for All (Urban) hnuaia hamthatna dawngtute tlawhin a kawm a ni. Governor hi Environment, Forest & Climate Change Minister Pu T.J. Lalnuntluanga, Champhai South bialtu MLA ni bawk bakah DC Champhai Pu James Lalrinchhana, SP Pu Lalrinpuia Varte leh Official dangten an tawiawm a ni. Governor Pu Hari Babu Kambhampati chuan Champhai Winery tlawh theia a awm chu lawmawm a tih thu sawiin, an hmalaknate engemawchen a lo hriat tawh thu a sawi a. Champhai District-a Winery pahnih lai a awm leh loneitute intelkhawmin an kalpui chu ropui a tih thu a sawi a. Grape chingtuten harsatna an tawh chu pawi a tih thu sawiin, Sawrkarin dan thar siama hma a la chu lawmawm a ti a. Wine siam chu food processing hnuaia a awm anih thu sawiin, agriculture product-te cheibawla siam danglam value addition chu hmalakna pawimawh tak a ni, a ti a. Tun aia nasaa huang zauh leh changtlung zawka kal tura Ministry of Food Processing Industries kaltlanga hmalakna an nei chu lawmawm a tih thu a sawi bawk. Governor chuan Grape chauh nilo thei dang sawr leh um theihte pawh ngaihvena huang zauh a tul thu a sawi a. An hmalak lehzelna turah duhsakna a hlan a, Mizoram mai nilo India rama loneitute tana entawntlak leh tihhmuhtu nih tum turin a chah a ni. Environment, Forest & Climate Change Minister Pu T.J. Lalnuntluanga chuan Champhai District chhunga loneitute hmalakna pawimawh tak grape sawngbawlna hmunhma Governor-in a hun hlu tak senga a tlawh chu lawmawm a ti a. Hun harsa tak paltlanga dan anga grape zawrhna tur dan thar Sawrkarin a siam thu sawiin, grape chingtuten hmabak eng tak an neih thu sawiin duhsakna a hlan a. Tun aia nasa zawka hma la a, ram ngaw humhalh nan kum tina lovah thin bansana lo nghet nei thei tura ngaihtuahna seng turin a chah a. Tun atanga reiloteah Sapthei sawngbawlna turte pawh buaipui tum anih thu sawiin, harsatna an neihte a hnena thlen hrehlo turin a chah a ni. Inkawmhona hun Packing Hall, Champhai Winery, Tlangsama hman hi Pu HS.Vanlalfakzuala, Chairman, Champhai Grape Growers Society (CGGS) chuan a kaihruai a. Pu Hrilchunglura, General Manager hnen atangin report ngaihthlak a ni a. Hnahlan Grape Growers and Processing Co-operative Society Limited hotute atangin thusawi ngaihthlak a ni bawk. Mizoram hi North East India-a grape thar awm chhun leh India rama grape thar tam 5-na niin, Champhai leh Hnahlan-ah Winery a awm a. CGGS enkawl Champhai Winery hian kum 14 hmel a hmu tawh a, an Grape sawngbawl hi Bangalore Blue variety niin, vawiin thlengin Grape quintal ,15,218 an lei tling tawh a, hemi atan hian Rs 5,78,41,160/- (cheng vaibelchhe nga maktaduai sarih nuai riat singli sangkhat za leh sawmruk) an seng tawh a ni. Kum 2010 atang khan Grape quintal 918 leiin bul an tan a, kum kalta khan quintal 1144.98 an lei tling a, an Grape lakte hi herin a umna zemah an um mek a ni. Kum 2007 khan Champhai Grape Growers Association (CGGA) tih thin chu Winery din anih dawn avangin Champhai Grape Growers Society (CGGS) ti a thlak niin, Firms & Society-ah an inziahlut a ni. MIP sum cheng nuai 83 (loan) hmanga bultan niin, he loan hi November ni 9, 2020 khan Sawrkar chuan rulh let ngai lo turin grant-ah a leh sak a ni. Champhai Grape Growers Society-ah hian Governing Board Member 15 awmin kum 2 danah inthlan thin a ni a. Tun dinhmunah hian Champhai Grape Growers Society-ah hian Grape chingtu member 134 awm mekin, Staff leh Worker mi 30, Executive Member 9 leh Office Bearer 6 an awm mek bawk a. Champhai Grape Growers Society hnuaiah hian Branch 9 awm mekin mumal taka inenkawlna kalpui thin a ni. CGGS hian Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MOFPI) kaltlangin project an kalpui mek a. DC Office kaltlangin Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) hnuaiah Commerce & Industries Department hnuaiah project dil mek a ni bawk a. Dan thar hnuaiah Winery License an nei fel tawh a, State pawn thlenga hralhchhuak thei turin hmachhawp an nei a ni. Champhai Winery a tlawh zawh hian Governor chuan BPL family-te tana a thlawna eirawngbawlna gas connection pekna scheme, Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) kaltlanga hamthatna dawngtu leh khawpuia cheng insak tanpuina scheme, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Housing for All (Urban) dawngtu Tlangsam ami te a tlawh a; scheme awmzia leh tangkainate a sawifiah a, an hmuh dan leh chhawr tangkai dante a zawt nghal bawk. reference: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati visits Champhai Tlangsam Winery 326/2022-2023 Aizawl, the 1st February 2023 : Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati, who is on a two-day tour of Champhai District visited the Tlangsam Winery on the outskirt of Champhai Town this evening. At the site, Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati was given an escorted tour to various units by the managing officers of the winery. Thereafter, a short program was held at B Remmawia Packing hall, Champhai Winery. Governor Hari Babu expressed his delight in visiting the factory started, owned, and managed by a society of farmers. He was particularly appreciative of having witness the production centre where the determined farmers themselves added value to their products. He congratulated the Champhai Grape Growers Society and the Hnahlan Grape Growers and Processing Co-operative Society Ltd. Governor welcomed the ambitious proposal to upgrade these wineries at Champhai and Hnahlan to accomodate the growing production of the Grapes in these areas. He extended his support for this proposal and if necessary, he agreed to discuss the matter with the authorities in the Ministry of Food Processing Industries(MoFPI). On behalf of Champhai Winery, Pu Hrilchunglura, General Manager, Champhai Grape Growers Society(GGGS) gave a report. The Winery was started in 2007. Champhai, February 1, 2023: Mizoram Governor Pu Hari Babu Kambhampati, who is on a two-day visit to Champhai, inspected the activities of Champhai Winery, Tlangsam, this afternoon, and also met the leaders of the Champhai Grape Growers Society and the Hnahlan Grape Growers and Processing Co-operative Society Limited. 5th State Level Task Force Meeting

At 11 AM today, the State Level Task Force (SLTF) on the National Railway Project held a meeting in the I&PR Conference Hall under the chairmanship of Task Force Chairman Pu. Zasanga, IPS (Rtd).

The meeting discussed land acquisition, forest clearance, the proposal for Khanrek Railway Station, and the construction of a railway station at Sihhmui.

Pu. V.P. Srivastava, Chief Engineer, NF Railways, Guwahati, presented a report on the work completed so far and said that the Final Location Survey (FLS) was continuing smoothly. He stated that the GPS, traversing, and topography survey between Bairabi and Sairang, covering 51.21 kms, had been completed. He also said that the Final Stacking Alignment, which began on 17 April 2010 from Bairabi and Hortoki, was targeted for completion by 31 May 2010.

To review the work done by NF Railways and to facilitate clearer progress on matters related to land acquisition and forest clearance, the concerned departments—Revenue, Forest, and Railways—decided to conduct a joint survey on 26 April 2010 under the leadership of the Kolasib Deputy Commissioner.

VICE CHAIRMAN OF HPC, PU LAWMAWMA TOCHHAWNG INAUGURATES RENOVATED LUNGLEI POLICE STATION BUILDING

1328/2023-2025 Lunglei; August 1, 2023: At 11:30 a.m. today, the renovated Lunglei Police Station Building (Ground Floor) was inaugurated by the chief guest, Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng, Vice Chairman, HPC Lunglei. The funds for the renovation of the building were received from the Lunglei High Powered Committee Fund. For the renovation of the ground floor and first floor, Rs. 15 lakh each was sanctioned from the HPC Fund. The ground floor, inaugurated today, was renovated using funds from 2022-2023. Rs. 15 lakh has also already been sanctioned for the renovation of the first floor for 2023-2024, so that the Police Department can continue the renovation work and the work can be started at any time.

The Lunglei Police Station building was built in 1991 and is located in the heart of Lunglei town; the building is now very old. Speaking at the inauguration ceremony of the renovated Police Station Building today, Pu Lawmawma said that Lunglei Police Station is a contender for the title of Best Police Station in India, and after being assessed on various criteria, its renovation into what could become the best police station building in India and the best in Mizoram is truly fitting. While congratulating the police, he said that even he himself would always remember this as something worthy of note.

Pu Lawmawma also said that it is admirable that the staff of Lunglei Police Station carried out the renovation work with a sense of ownership, and that working together with deserving people is very pleasant. He further urged the Lunglei Police to strive to become the best in India, especially in traffic management within their jurisdiction. He also expressed his wish that the police station should be a place where the public can approach without hesitation and where they can confidently bring their problems and grievances, and that with the new building, the PS staff too may continue to receive those who come to them in a pleasant and welcoming manner.

The inauguration ceremony for the renovated building was held at the police station courtyard. The meeting was chaired by Pu K. Beihmotaosa MPS, Addl. SP Lunglei, while Pu H. Ramthlengliana, IPS, DIG (SR), and Pi Ramdinliani IAS

raw_text:
UNANNOUNCED VISIT TO SOME OFFICES IN SIAHA DC OFFICE

Deputy Commissioner, Siaha District, Pu Bhupesh Chaudhary IAS, made an unannounced visit to some offices this morning. Pu Bhupesh said that his “surprised visit” was not meant to find fault with the functioning of offices or to embarrass anyone, but to understand how the various offices are being run and to listen to the difficulties they face. He also said that he is always keeping a close watch on the working style and procedures of the offices under his jurisdiction, and that staff who neglect duty and do not want to work properly will face serious consequences; he wanted them to know this.

The offices visited today were: ITI (Industrial Training Institute), Excise & Narcotics Office, Mizofed, Printing & Stationery Depot, and FCS & Consumer Affairs Godown. Surprise visits are usually conducted whenever time permits, and all offices and educational institutions under the Government of Mizoram are planned to be visited. During today’s surprise visit, Pu Amol Srivastava IAS, Assistant Commissioner, Pu H. Zonunmawia, Election Officer, and Pu N. Vabeiratlua, DIPRO accompanied the Deputy Commissioner.

reference: DISTRICT TASK FORCE COMMITTEE HELD EMERGENCY MEETING ON COVID-19 AT SIAHA District Task Force,Siaha mulled over how to take preventive measures against Covid-19 pandemic in the emergency meeting held, here at Siaha. District Magistrate had already issued prohibitory order on last Friday(7/3/2020), the order prohibited Cross- border movement between Myanmar and India through passages/roads that linked Myanmar and 10 villages within Siaha district namely: : Lopu, Chapi, Khaikhy, Zyhno,Lodaw, Lomasu, Iana, Siasi, Laki and Khopai village. The Same order highlighted that Check points will be set up at 3 villages namely: Kaochao, Tlapi and Tipi Ferry which located at Inter District Border. In pursuant to the said prohibitory Order, Siaha BDO and Tipa BDO have left for those 10 villages to call for GramSabha meeting and to sensitize about Covid-19 and Prohibitory Order. Today's meeting resolved that villagers of those 10 villages be requested to form a joint committee comprising of Church, NGOs and Village council to vigil over border passage/road that linked their respective village and Myanmar.The meeting also resolved that MADC Forest Guard and India Army stationed at villages located India-Myanmar Border be requested to help proposed village's Joint committee in their vigilant works on Border road/passage. Today's meeting also decided that on the 13th&14th March,2020 a Team comprising Medical officials, Leaders of NGOs, Joint VC members, Police personnel and DC office staff will visited those 13 villages and witness preventive measures taken by each village and carry out sensitization campaign as well. CMO & DMS informed the meeting that there was only one Thermal Infra Red Sensor and 15 Personal Protection Equipments (PPE) presently at Siaha; and 2 TIRS will arrive shortly. TIRS and Self Reporting Format will be placed at check points; and by using TIRS leh Self reporting format; suspected Covid-19 infected travellers will be identified and quarantine for 20 days. hypothesis: At Siaha, the District Task Force Committee held an emergency meeting on COVID-19. At 2:00 PM today, the District Task Force Committee held an emergency meeting in the DC Conference Hall to discuss COVID-19 and held a detailed meeting on how Siaha district can stay safe from COVID-19. On 7/3/2020, the District Magistrate had already ordered the closure of the 10 villages in Siaha district—Lopu, Chapi, Khaikhy, Zyhno, Lodaw, Lomasu, Iana, Siasi, Laki, and Khopai—as well as the road connecting to Myanmar. In addition, orders had already been issued to set up check posts at the three inter-district border crossing points: Kaochao, Tipi Ferry, and Tlapi. Today, Siaha BDO and Tipa BDO also went out to these 13 villages to conduct a Gram Sabha and a sensitization campaign. The meeting today also resolved to request each of these 13 villages to form a joint committee of the church, NGOs, and VC, and these joint committees were also asked to monitor the roads/paths connecting their villages to Myanmar. It was also resolved to invite the MADC Forest Department and the Indian Army stationed in the border-area villages to assist them. On 13 and 14 March 2020, a joint team of medical personnel, NGO leaders, joint VC leaders, police, and the DC office will visit these 13 villages to inspect how they are monitoring the routes connecting to Myanmar for the prevention of COVID-19, and will immediately continue the sensitization campaign. At present, the Siaha Medical Office has only one Thermal Infra Red Sensor for detecting fever and 15 Personal Protection Equipment (PPE), and it has been reported that 2 more TIRS are on the way. These TIRS will be placed at the three check posts. In addition to the TIRS, the medical department will also place Self Reporting Forms at all three checkpoints. Based on the TIRS and self-reporting forms, suspected travelers who may be carrying COVID-19 and those entering Siaha district will be kept separately for 20 days.

In addition, orders had already been issued to set up check posts at the three inter-district border crossing points: Kaochao, Tipi Ferry, and Tlapi. Today, Siaha BDO and Tipa BDO also went out to these 13 villages to conduct a Gram Sabha and a sensitization campaign. The meeting today also resolved to request each of these 13 villages to form a joint committee of the church, NGOs, and VC, and these joint committees were also asked to monitor the roads/paths connecting their villages to Myanmar. It was also resolved to invite the MADC Forest Department and the Indian Army stationed in the border-area villages to assist them. On 13 and 14 March 2020, a joint team of medical personnel, NGO leaders, joint VC leaders, police, and the DC office will visit these 13 villages to inspect how they are monitoring the routes connecting to Myanmar for the prevention of COVID-19, and will immediately continue the sensitization campaign. Based on the TIRS and self-reporting forms, suspected travelers who may be carrying COVID-19 and those entering Siaha district will be kept separately for 20 days.

Hei hi rahbi hmasa ber chu a ni. Hei hi kan ti zo tawh anih chuan, hetah hian enfiahna ka dah thei; thil hmasa ber chu zawh a ni tawh. A rahbi pahnihna chu enge ni? Chuti anih loh chuan, in nung thei lo a, in kal zel thei lo a, in nun chu Kristian angin in vawngṭha thei lo. Nitin in kan nitin chaw leh kan tuinung ang in Krista chu kan chên ngei ngei tur a ni, ei tur thil engemaw leh in tur thil engemaw kan nei ngei tur a ni. Zing ah kan inhmuh apiang in chibai kan inbûkna atan “Zing ṭha!” inti ngawt lovin “I ei tawh em?” tiin i inzawt zawk ang u. Chutiang chibai inbûkna chu ka thlang zawk daih mai. Tukin zing ah hian i ei tawh em, unaupa? Tukin zingah hian engemaw i in tawh em, unaunu. Thenkhat chuan vawiin ah chaw ṭha tak vawi thum in ei tawh tiin min chhang thei a. reference: What then is the way to possess the good land? It is not so simple. Let us enumerate and review the steps. First of all, we must enjoy Christ as the redeeming lamb. We must receive Christ as our Savior. We must pass the judgment of God. This is the first step. If we have done this, we can put a check here; the first item has been passed. What is the second step? We must leave Egypt and enjoy Christ as our daily manna, as our daily life-supply. Of course, we cannot take food without drinking water; so at the same time we must enjoy Christ as the rock with the living water flowing forth. We enjoy the manna and we enjoy the rock with the living water. Do you have such an experience day by day? Many of you can boldly say that you do. Every day you enjoy Christ as your food and as your drink. Otherwise, you could not live, you could not go on, you could not maintain your life as a Christian. Day by day, we must enjoy Christ as our daily food and our living water; we must have something to eat and something to drink. Whenever we meet in the morning, instead of greeting one another with “Good morning!” let us ask “Have you eaten?” I do prefer such a greeting. Have you eaten this morning, brother? Have you drunk something this morning, sister? Some of you can answer that you have had three good meals today. Praise the Lord! We must tell people that day by day we are feeding on Christ. We are eating Christ and we are drinking Christ. If we have this experience, we can check this also.

raw_text:
CHAMPHAI DISTRICT CONSULTATIVE COMMITTEE (DCC) / DISTRICT LEVEL REVIEW COMMITTEE (DLRC) MEETING No.7432/2020-2021

The Champhai District Consultative Committee (DCC) / District Level Review Committee (DLRC), chaired by Pi Maria C.T. Zuali, Champhai DC, met today at the DC Conference Hall and reviewed the activities of various banks and stakeholders within Champhai District RD Block 2 up to the end of the September 2020 quarter. The Potential Credit Linked Plan (PLP) for Champhai District for 2021-2022, prepared by NABARD, was also presented by Deputy Commissioner Pi Maria C.T. Zuali.

Pi Maria C.T. Zuali said that banking facilities need to be made accessible to everyone, and that wider awareness campaigns are urgently needed so that people can fully benefit from banking services. She urged bank officials to prepare and translate important documents and application forms into Mizo so that the public can better understand how to use banking services and become more aware of the benefits available through banks. She also called on banks to continue supporting the poor and vulnerable so that they can receive benefits and improve their livelihoods. Referring to the Credit Deposit Ratio, which shows a large gap between deposits and advances, she said it was a matter of concern and urged banks to work more actively to achieve a better Credit Deposit Ratio. She also reminded loan borrowers to repay their loans on time, and said that in cases of default, the DC Office would fully cooperate with bankers in pursuing recovery.

At the meeting, Pu L. Lawmvela, Lead District Manager (LDM), SBI Lead Bank Office, Champhai, first welcomed the attendees and then presented a review of the work and activities of the various banks in Champhai District up to the end of the September 2020 quarter, followed by discussion of future plans.

reference: Meghalaya State Planning Board Chairman calls on Chief Minister No.252/2021-2022 Aizawl the 18th August, 2021: Chief Minister Pu Zoramthanga, Chairman of State Planning Board was called on by State Planning Board Chairman Pu Lambor Malngiang (MLA/MDC), Meghalaya today at the formerâ€™s office where they discussed important issues relating to economic development for both states. The Meghalaya State Planning Board Chairman expressed his gratitude for the outstanding hospitality shown by Mizoram and hoped that the bond between the two states would continue to flourish. Speaking of how he works closely with Mizo community and many sub-tribes of Mizoram in his constituency, he expressed his optimism for an enduring friendship and partnership in all sectors. Mizoram Chief Minister echoed the importance of nurturing good relations between the two states, and said that should any situation arise where Mizoram can assist Meghalaya in the development of its economy, Mizoram shall do its best. After his meeting with the Chief Minister, Pu Lambor Malngiang met with Mizoram Planning Board Vice Chairman Pu H. Rammawi followed by a meeting with NGO leaders of the state. He was accompanied by Dr. Krishna Chauhan, Expert Member (Economist) Meghalaya State Planning Board and Pu Enrich GL Nongbri, Law Department, Govt. of Meghalaya. Attachment Loading attachment...

raw_text:
MIZORAM AND MEGHALAYA PLANNING BOARD LEADERS MEET  
No.1907/2021-2022  
Aizawl, 18th August, 2021: Pu Lambor Malngiang, Chairman of the Meghalaya State Planning Board, who came to Aizawl for a one-day visit, and Pu H. Rammawi, Vice Chairman of the Mizoram State Planning Board, met today at Pu Rammawi’s office and discussed matters concerning cooperation between the two states for future development.

Pu H. Rammawi explained the broad functions of the Mizoram State Planning Board and told Pu Lambor that it was a matter of joy that Mizoram and Meghalaya have such good cooperation for the unity of the Northeastern states.

The Mizoram State Planning Board Vice Chairman was accompanied by Principal Adviser-cum-Addl. Secretary, Planning & Programme Implementation Department Dr. Lalrinchhana and Pi Chingthanmawi Guite, Deputy Adviser-cum-Deputy Secretary, Planning & Programme Implementation Department. Pu Lambhor Malngiang was accompanied by Dr. Krishna Chauhan, Expert Member, and Enrich GL Nongbri of the Law Department, Government of Meghalaya.

After the leaders of the two state Planning Boards concluded their meeting, they immediately held another meeting with NGO leaders.

THE PRIESTHOOD WITH URIM AND THUMMIM

The second aspect of the order of worship is the priesthood under the anointing of the Urim and Thummim. What is the priesthood? This is a wonderful and glorious thing. The priesthood includes fellowship with the Lord, life, and service in His presence. The priesthood is the gathering of the people who continually have fellowship with the Lord. They live in complete union with the Lord and serve in His presence. In this way they live, walk, and do everything. If we have fellowship with the Lord, and if we live every day and at all times in complete union with the Lord, dwelling in this living fellowship and serving, then in our conduct we are the priesthood.

source: Governor Hari Babu leh ITCA hotupa in Mizorama zirlai thiam zual te tana space technology zir theih dan sawi dun 1070/2022-2023 Aizawl, the 28th June 2022: Vawiin chawhma khan Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati leh Dr SK Prasad, founder member and advisory council member, Indian Technology Congress Association ( ITCA), Bangalore te chu Raj Bhavan-ah an inkawm a. He hunah hian Mizorama zirlai thiam filawr te zinga space technology zir duh thlan chhuah dan tur leh an zir theih dan tur te an sawi dun a ni. Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati chuan Mizorama zirlaite chu lehkha thiam thei tak leh hmundanga zirlaite el phaka thluak tha an ni tih a sawi a. Space technology pawh a zirna kawng a inhawn phawt chuan hlawhtling takin an zir thei turah angai tih a sawi a ni. Governor chuan Dr SK Prasad leh a thawhna hmuna thuneituten Mizoramah zirlai te tan Space Technology zir theihna hun remchang an rawn zawn sak chu lawmawm a tih thu a sawi a. Hemi kawngah hian ITCA hotute chuan Higher & Technical Education Department, Mizoram University, NIT Mizoram, Polytechnics, Science & Technology Department leh Science Teachers Association Of Mizoram berawn se. Anni nena indawrna kaltlang hian zirlai thiam thei zual zinga space technology zir duhte thlanchhuah a awlsam a rin thu a sawi a ni. Dr SK Prasad chuan Prime Minister hmathlir angin India thalaite chu space technology lamah thiamna sang zawk nei tur leh India ram chu a hmahruaitu a nih theih nan chher hriam mek an ni a ti a. He hmalakna kal zelah hian zirlai team 75 te chu kumina project 75 thawk zo hman turin Students' Satellites 75 project hnuaiah satellite te chi(mini satellite) siam turin thlan an ni dawn an a ti. He project-ah hian India rama zirlaite zawng zawng an inel dawn a team 75 thlan an ni dawn a ti a. He project-ah hian Mizorama zirlaite tan pawh tel theihna hun a inhawng thei dawn niin a sawi a ni. Dr Prasad chuan a lo kal chhan tak chu Higher Secondary atanga University Degree zirlaite tan Space Technology zirna an kalpui mek chu Mizorama zirlaite rawn hmelhriat tir a ni a ti a. Hemi kawngah hian Governor leh state sawrkar hotute thlawpna a rawn ngen bakah a bikin science lam zirna kaihhnawiha hotute thawhpuiah a rawn sawm tih a sawi bawk a ni. reference: Governor Hari Babu and ITCA member discuss opportunities for students to learn space technology 102/2022-2023 Aizawl, the 28th June 2022: Dr SK Prasad, founder member and advisory council member, Indian Technology Congress Association ( ITCA) had called on Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati at the Raj Bhavan this forenoon. In this meeting, he and Governor discussed the opportunities for the students of higher secondary school, college and university in Mizoram to learn space technology. As proposed by his eminent guest, Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati welcomed the idea of selecting students with a scientific temper to have a preliminary introduction to space science with the option to continue the advanced study depending on their performance in studies. In this regard, he advised Dr SK Prasad and the institutions he represented to have close coordination with the authorities of Higher & Technical Education Department, Mizoram University, NIT Mizoram, Polytechnics, Science & Technology Department and Science Teachers Association Of Mizoram. Dr SK Prasad apprised the Governor of their initiatives in teaching the teams of students and assigning them important science projects like making mini satellites and other space technology. He explained the importance given to horning entrepreneurship skills of the students selected in this model of learning. He told Governor that his purpose of visiting is identifying the institutions with whom they will have a series of correspondences to initiate enrollment of the students in the program. hypothesis: Governor Hari Babu and the head of ITCA discuss ways to teach space technology to talented students in Mizoram 1070/2022-2023 Aizawl, June 28, 2022: This morning, Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati and Dr. SK Prasad, founder member and advisory council member of the Indian Technology Congress Association (ITCA), Bangalore, met at Raj Bhavan. During the meeting, they discussed how to select talented students in Mizoram who want to study space technology and how they can be trained. Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati said that students in Mizoram are very capable, intelligent, and able to compete with students from other places. He said that if the path to learning space technology is opened, they will be able to study it successfully. The Governor said he was pleased that Dr. SK Prasad and the authorities at his organization had come forward to look for a suitable opportunity to provide space technology education for students in Mizoram. In this regard, the ITCA leaders should coordinate with the Higher & Technical Education Department, Mizoram University, NIT Mizoram, Polytechnics, the Science & Technology Department, and the Science Teachers Association of Mizoram. Through discussions with them, it will be easier to select talented students who want to study space technology, he said. Dr. SK Prasad said that, as envisioned by the Prime Minister, India’s youth are being sharpened and trained to gain higher expertise in space technology so that India can become a leader in this field. As part of this initiative, 75 student teams will be selected to build mini satellites under the Students’ Satellites 75 project, with the aim of completing 75 projects this year, he said. Under this project, teams from across India will compete, and 75 teams will be selected, he said. He added that this project may also open opportunities for students in Mizoram to participate. Dr. Prasad said that the main reason for his visit was to introduce to students in Mizoram the space technology education currently being carried out for students from higher secondary level to university degree level. In this regard, he also requested the Governor and state government leaders for support and invited those involved in science education to cooperate with him. Attachment Loading attachment...
