reference: CHAMPHAI DISTRICT TASK FORCE ON CORONA VIRUS OUTBREAK HELD MEETING In pursuance of the decision made by Mizoram State Level Task Force on Mitigation of Corona Virus, Champhai District Task Force on Corona Virus was formed recently and held its first meeting at DC Conference Hall, yesterday. The meeting was presided over by Pu SL Naveen, IAS Deputy Commissioner Champhai. Given its strategic location, Champhai district being located nearby International Border, the meeting mentioned the needs for proper medical screening at Zokhawthar and restriction on movement particularly travellers based on their travelling history. To boost up the preventive measures, the meeting highlighted the importance of fostering better coordination with the neighbouring district administration of Myanmar. The meeting decided to organize awareness campaigns for villages nearby border areas and preparation of isolation ward for quarantine in case any suspect is detected. CMO Office was assigned to prepare budget encompassing all requirements for further submission to the higher authority. At the border Town of Zokhawthar, Government of Mizoram has been monitoring the situation and is conducting Medical Screening since the 4th of February 2020 with proper Self Reporting Form. raw_text:
CHAMPHAI DISTRICT TASK FORCE ON CORONA VIRUS OUTBREAK MEETING

In view of the Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV) disease spreading in China and other countries around the world, the District Task Force on Corona Virus Outbreak was formed to ensure the safety and preparedness of Champhai District. Its first meeting was held this afternoon in the DC Conference Hall, chaired by Deputy Commissioner Pu SL Naveen, IAS.

At the meeting, it was stated that since Champhai District is located on an international border, caution is necessary to prevent the further spread of the Novel Coronavirus. The meeting also urged those who frequently travel across the border and traders to be careful in and around the areas where the disease is spreading. During the meeting, the restrictions on human movement and livestock movement were also discussed.

It was also stated that there is a need for close coordination and cooperation with the districts in Myanmar bordering Champhai District. The District Task Force on Coronavirus Outbreak said that the villages along the border should be visited and the public given wider awareness, and that health screening should be carried out for those entering through the border, with any suspected cases being traced and investigated. It was also decided that an Isolation Ward should be set up at Champhai District Hospital, and that the required budget should be prepared quickly and submitted to the higher authorities.

The District Level Task Force on Corona Virus Outbreak was constituted in line with the decision of the State Level Task Force on Mitigation of Corona Virus, formed by the Mizoram State Health Minister and officials of the H&FW Department on January 30, 2020, to take action in each district. Medical screening has been started at Zokhawthar in Champhai District from February 4, 2020, and the work of checking details of visitors and screening as necessary has been carried out, along with the introduction of a proper Self Reporting Form.

The Champhai District Task Force on Corona Virus Outbreak has also set up the mobile numbers 8588009756 / 9436376607 for those in need to contact.

Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrated in grand style

This morning at the AR Ground, Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) was observed, with Deputy Chief Minister Pu Tawnluia as the chief guest. Speaking on the occasion, chief guest Pu Tawnluia said that in honor of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who played a major role in building India’s unity, the Government of India declared October 31 as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day), he said.

The Deputy Chief Minister said that Rashtriya Ekta Diwas has been observed since 2014, and today is the sixth observance, he said. In 1917, after hearing the words of India’s Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel dedicated himself fully to the cause of India and worked courageously, earning him the title “Iron Man of India,” he said. He said that when the British were about to leave India, he worked to ensure that more than 500 princely states across India could be united under India.

Chief guest Pu Tawnluia called on everyone to work for the nation and to continue preserving unity, following the example of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, one of the key figures in India’s freedom struggle. Chief Secretary Pu Lalnunmawia Chuaungo administered the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas pledge to all those present for the event.

Nine contingents—Assam Rifles, BSF, 1st Battalion MAP, 3rd Battalion MAP, 5th IR Battalion, Home Guard, 225 Battalion CRPF, One Mizo Air Squadron NCC, and 20 Mizo Independent Company NCC—took part in the parade. The Parade Commander was Inspector PC Vanlalsawma of MAP, and the Assam Rifles Band Party also played the National Anthem.

As part of the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebration, 500 schoolchildren took part in the Run for Unity at 7:00 a.m., starting from Sikulpuikawn and Chanmari, and gathered together at the AR Ground.

source: MIZORAM POLICE PRESS STATEMENT 566/2023-2024 Mizoram police media cell chuan Digital Payment System chungchanga mipuite hnena thurawn a hnuaia mi ang hian a ti chhuak : DIGITAL PAYMENT INBUMNA CHUNGCHANGA THURAWN : Digital Payment Systems hman kan uar chhoh viau laiin hemi kaihhnawiha inbumna pawh nasa takin Mizoramah ngei pawh a sang chho chak hie a ni. Hetianga internet khawvela bum tur zawng ho hian rinhlelh nachang hre lo leh bum awlsam tur zawngin, inbum dan thar an hmu chhuak reng bawk. Tunah hian Mizorama Cyber Crime case ziah luh zinga 75% aia tarn hi 'online financial fraud' kaihhnawih a ni. Chuvangin hetianga inbumna laka kan himna atan Mizoram Poice chuan a hnuaia tarlan ang hian mipuite a ngen a ni: I banking password, OTP, Debit Card/Credit Card details te tumah hrilh suh. Pawisa dawngtu tur i nihin eng QR Code mah scan suh. Pawisa thawn chhuaktu tur tan lo chuan engmah scan a ngai lo. Phishing scammer te hian i Bank leh UPI information pawimawh ruksak che an turn reng tih hria la, email leh website lemah te, link hriat chian lohah te lut mai mai suh ang che. Online-a thil i lei dawnin Search Engine atanga product zawn hi a him tawk lo thin a, chuvangin online shopping website hriat chian saah ngei thil enin lei thin ang che. Engmah thawk mang lova pawisa hlawh theihna te, pawisa dah punna hlawk lutuk leh him si tih ang chi, thil tha uchuak lutuk ang hi inbumna a ni tlangpui tih hria ang che. Awlsam leh rang taka Loan pe chhuak thei anga insawi application leh website lakah fimkhur ang che. Loan pe turin mimal thil pawimawh tinreng an dil a, heng te hi a hnua blackmail lehna atan te an hmang thin a ni. Loan App i hmang a nih pawhin RBI phalna nei an ni ngei em tih chian ang che. Police/Army anga insawi a, thil tlawm tak taka tiral duh anga online-a inzuar thinte hi misual an ni tlangpui tih hre bawk ang che. Online a sum chet velna tur thil khawih reng rengin theihtawpa fimkhur turin mipuite kan chah nawn leh a, hetianga bumna tuartu i nih chuan Cyber Helpline 1930-ah emaw, www.cybercrime.gov.in ah emaw complaint i thehlut thei a ni. A HNUAIA TARLAN ANG HI www.cybercrime.gov.in AH COMPLAINT THEHLUH DAN A NI. 1. Mobile leh Computer browser (Google, Safari, etc.) eng atang pawhin www.cybercrime.gov.in i lut ang. 2. Box sen pahnih a lo awm ang a, "File Complaint' tih zawkah i lut ang. 3. "I Accept" tih a lo lang ang a, i lo click ang. 4. "Report Cyber Crime" tih i hmu ang a, i click ang. 5. Page thar a lo inhawng ang a, "Click here for new user" tihah lutin, form i fill-up ang. 6. Account i logged-in hnuah cyber crime category thlanna a lo awm ang a, i report duh category i thlang ang. 7. Online transaction hmanga bum i nih chuan "Online Financial Fraud" i thlang ang. 8. Pawisa thawn chhuaktu bank account details i chhu lut ang. 9. UPI hmanga pawisa thawn a nih chuan i UPI App hman (BHIM, Gpay, Paytm, etc.) i thlang ang. 10. I pawisa thawn chhuahna Transaction ID i chhu lut ang. Hriattur: Transaction ID hi digit 12 a ni a, pawisa i thawn a bank atanga SMS i dawn thin angah khan a awm. 11. I account-ah i hriatlohvin pawisa a lo lut a nih chuan "Credit Transaction Details" tihah khan a tul angin i fill up bawk dawn nia. 12. Hetianga a ml i tih zawh hnu hian "Save as Draft and Next" tih i thlang ang. 13. A phek dawt lehah a tuartu/a complaint tu details i fill up ang a, "Save as Draft and Next" i thlang leh ang. 15. "I Agree" i thlang ang a, chumi hnuah "Confirm and Submit" i thlang leh dawn nia. Cyber fraudsters are finding new methods to dupe vulnerable and unsuspecting citizens. Online financial frauds account for more than 75% of all cyber-crimes reported in the State. With an aim to prevent financial losses to the general public through online frauds, Mizoram Police once again appeals to public to take following precautions: 1. Never share your Banking password, OTP (one time password) or Debit/Credit Card details with others. 2. Never scan QR Code, when you are to receive money. It is only required for transferring money to other accounts. 3. Beware of phishing scams trying to steal your Banking or UPI information. Look out for fake emails and websites, that try to collect information and do not click on unknownâ€™unfamiliar links. 4. Always use familiar websites for online shopping rather than shopping by searching products on search engines. Search results can be misleading and may lead to malicious websites. 5. Ignore advertisements/deals, if they claim that you can earn money with little or no work or you can make money on an investment with little or no risk. If an offer seems too good to be true, it is most likely to be a scam. 6. Beware of fake loan apps that provide quick and easy loans. Such illegal apps will seek a variety of information and permissions from applicants, which is then misused to blackmail them later. If using digital loan app, please ensure that it has RBI authorization. 7. Beware of fraudsters, who impersonate as army/police personnel advertising cheap items online. MIZORAM POLICE PRESS STATEMENT 566/2023-2024

The Mizoram Police Media Cell issues the following advisory to the public regarding Digital Payment Systems:

ADVISORY ON DIGITAL PAYMENT FRAUD:

As the use of Digital Payment Systems has increased, fraud related to them has also been rising rapidly, even in Mizoram. Those who want to cheat people on the internet are constantly finding new ways to deceive unsuspecting people and make fraud easier. At present, more than 75% of the cyber crime cases registered in Mizoram are related to online financial fraud. Therefore, for our safety against such fraud, Mizoram Police requests the public as follows:

Do not share your banking password, OTP, Debit Card/Credit Card details with anyone. If you are the recipient of money, do not scan any QR code. Unless you are the one sending money, there is no need to scan anything. Be aware that phishing scammers are always trying to steal your bank and UPI information; do not enter into unfamiliar emails, websites, or links. When buying things online, searching for products through search engines is not always safe, so always check and buy only from trusted online shopping websites. Be aware that offers such as earning money without doing any work, very high returns on deposits, or unusually attractive deals are generally scams. Be careful of applications and websites that claim to provide loans easily and quickly. To get a loan, they ask for all kinds of personal information, which they later use for blackmail. If you use a loan app, make sure it has RBI approval. Also be aware that people who claim to be police/army personnel and sell things online at very cheap prices are generally criminals.

We once again urge the public to be extremely careful in all matters involving online money transactions. If you become a victim of such fraud, you can file a complaint at the Cyber Helpline 1930 or at www.cybercrime.gov.in.

THE FOLLOWING ARE THE STEPS TO FILE A COMPLAINT AT www.cybercrime.gov.in:

1. From any mobile or computer browser (Google, Safari, etc.), go to www.cybercrime.gov.in.

3. "I Accept" will appear; click it.
4. You will see "Report Cyber Crime"; click it.
